summary: Added a DSpark-specific --speculative-dspark-lora-path that creates a draft-local, pinned LoRA manager and routes every DSpark draft forward through that adapter without altering target-model LoRA routing. This is a verified single-adapter foundation, not the complete request-selectable multi-adapter proposal.

tests.what_was_measured: Nine CPU tests covering draft-local manager construction, deterministic pinned adapter identity, fixed adapter routing on every request in a DSpark draft batch, and existing DSpark startup behavior.
Three GPU tests for speculative verification LoRA segment metadata, including eager and CUDA-graph layouts.
Real MI355X execution of the LoRA fused MoE kernel against the test's independent PyTorch numerical reference.
Formatter/linter availability only; neither ruff nor black is installed in the pinned interpreter. git diff --check passed.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0. Raw logs: reports/j-db7867ac91bd/raw/gpu_lora_spec_verify.txt and gpu_lora_numerical.txt.
remaining_limitations: Only one fixed DSpark draft adapter can be selected at server startup. Per-request selection, dynamic load/unload, and batching multiple draft adapters remain unimplemented.

No public DSpark base checkpoint plus compatible stage-2 LoRA adapter was available in the prepared runtime, so an end-to-end DSpark model serving run and acceptance-rate comparison were not performed.
The qualified tiny Llama transport fixture cannot validate DSpark architecture or draft-adapter semantics and therefore was not used as substitute evidence.
CUDA graph integration follows the existing LoRA manager path and GPU metadata tests passed, but a full DSpark CUDA graph with real DSpark adapter weights remains unverified.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
